name: The Positive-Overlap Rooted Factor Has a Canonical Saturation
statement: For the 621-concept rooted factor $K$ and its one-concept endpoint repair $v$, let $F=\{0,\ldots,11\}\cup\{24,\ldots,36\}$, $J=\{1,2,36\}$, and $A_J=\{x\in Q_F:x|_J\ne v|_J\}$. Then $A_J$ peels relatively to $K$. Thus failure of the canonical four-relative-order recovery for $K$ does not prevent saturation from its endpoint repair. Applying the two-overlap square construction to $K$, $K\cup\{v\}$, and $A_J$ after translating the root to zero produces a rooted factor of order $29,361,372$.
proof: Split the coordinates outside $J$ into the common direction and the two private blocks of the explicit factor. Every word of $K$ has one private block zero. The full private cube peels to the union of those two coordinate subcubes because the complement is a product of corner-peelable punctured cubes. Taking a product with the punctured three-cube on $J$ and the common edge gives a relative peeling from $A_J$ to an intermediate family $L$. A verified finite order supplies the remaining 63,877 deletions from $|L|=64,498$ to $K$. The repaired family $W=K\cup\{v\}$ peels to the root and relatively to $K$; its unique acquired support is $J$, giving the required shadow intersection and ample union with $A_J$. The two-overlap transfer theorem therefore yields the rooted factor, and the section cardinalities give the stated order.
